$comment: Cross-language contract fixture for the MCP server name rule.
The rule is implemented twice, independently: MCP_CONNECTION_NAME_PATTERN in
packages/shared/src/types/mcp-connection.ts (control plane, rejects on write) and
sanitizeMcpServerName in packages/vm-agent/internal/acp/mcp_server_names.go (vm-agent,
falls back to positional naming rather than writing a hostile value into a TOML key or
an env var name).
Both implementations consume THIS file in their tests, so the two cannot drift (rule 23).
If you change one, this fixture will fail on the other side.
Note the two differ in DISPOSITION, not in the rule: TS rejects an invalid name with a 400,
Go substitutes a safe positional name. Both must agree on which names are valid, and both
normalize by trimming and lowercasing before judging.
The `urls` block pins the SECOND rule implemented twice: validateMcpConnectionUrl in
apps/api/src/services/mcp-connections.ts and normalizeMcpServers in
packages/vm-agent/internal/server/mcp_servers.go. These drifted in review: TS accepted
http://localhost/mcp (no port) while Go required an explicit port, and Go's rejection fails
the WHOLE create-agent-session request, so one saved row would have broken every session
for that scope.
The `headerNames` block pins the THIRD rule implemented twice: MCP_CONNECTION_HEADER_NAME_PATTERN
in packages/shared/src/types/mcp-connection.ts (control plane, rejects on write) and
ValidMcpHeaderName in packages/vm-agent/internal/acp/mcp_servers.go (vm-agent, rejects the
create-agent-session request). Both judge the exact string with no normalization; the control
plane trims user input before judging. The charset is what mcp-remote accepts in
`--header name:value` and what TOML accepts as a bare key.
`headerNames.reserved` pins MCP_CONNECTION_RESERVED_HEADER_NAMES (TS) to reservedMcpHeaderNames
in packages/vm-agent/internal/acp/mcp_servers.go: names the HTTP client or MCP transport sets
itself. Both sides compare case-insensitively and must hold exactly this list.
